sentences.text: POINT No.1 and 2: These points are inter linked with each other hence taken up together in order to avoid repetition and to have the brevity in the judgment.
.13. In the case on hand, the LAO has acquired the property in Sy. No. 83, while making reference to the Court the measurement shown as 1 acre 10.50 guntas of dry land of Kannalli village.
The copy of the award furnished to the Court discloses that the LAO has acquired only 3 acres of land and passed the consent award as on 29.01.2014.
Thereafter, in view of the dispute between the parties, the case has been referred to the Court.
Even copy of the L.A.C. No.45/2015 mahazar discloses that the LAO has acquired the land to the extent of 3 acres only in Sy.No.83 to form "Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout".
Hence, the extent of property acquired in this case is only 3 acres of land.
The claimants 3 and 4 as well as claimants 19 and 9 were not disputed the extent of land measuring 3 acres acquired by the respondent.

Hence,
undisputed and admitted facts in this case is that the LAO / respondent has acquired only 3 acres of land.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
.14. In this case, the claimants 3 and 4 along with claimant No.5 claim that the acquired property belongs to them.
However, the claimant No. 19 and 9 claim that they have purchased the said property and they are the owners of the said property and they being the owners of the property when the property has been acquired, they are entitled for the compensation involved in this case.
Accordingly claimed that the property acquired by the LAO is their property as western portion of the property in Sy. No. 83 has been acquired.
It is undisputed fact that the boundaries will prevail over extent or anything and when the specific boundary has been given and if the boundaries are undisputed, then the said boundaries has to be accepted in order to identify the property.
In view of these facts mere dismissal of the Interlocutory Application in the suit filed by the claimants 1 to 3 in O.S. No. 768/2016 and M.A.
No.48/2007 as per Ex.P.38 and Ex.P.71 respectively, cannot be accepted that the claimants 9 and 19 are in possession of acquired property.
.25. In the case on hand, the claimants 9 and 19 nowhere claimed that they have purchased any property from claimants 3 to 5.
Therefore, in the case on hand, the claimants 9 and 19 failed to prove that they are the owners of the acquired property or they are in possession of the said property.
When there is no execution of sale deed in respect of 14 acres 15 guntas of land in Sy. No. 83, how the said T.M. Rangegowda has acquired the right, title and interest over the said property, so that he can agree to sell the said property to claimant No.9 or 33 Vunduvalli Satyanarayana.
Even if it is accepted that there is a sale agreement dated 13.12.2006 by T.M. Rangegowda in favour of Vunduvalli Satyanarayana, it is for the Vunduvalli Satyanarayana to enforce the said sale agreement but why the said agreement has not been enforced by Vundavally sathyanarayana is without any explanation.
Admittedly the Final Notification regarding acquisition of property in Sy. No. 83 has been issued as on 18.02.2010, which is subsequent to the aforesaid 2 sale agreements.
In the case on hand, these claimants 9 and 19 namely Vunduvalli Satyanarayana and Gopinath Naidu suppressed or withhold the material document before the Court.
Even there is no material on record before the Court to show execution of any sale agreement by T.M. Rangegowda in favour of Vunduvalli Satyanarayana as on 13.12.2006.
.30.
There is no material on record to show that T.M. Rangegowda has got executed the registered sale deed and thereby he acquired valid right, title and interest over the property.
Therefore, there is not even a prima facie material on record to show that T.M. Rangegowda has acquired any valid right,
title and interest over the property in Sy. No.83 measuring 14 acres 15 guntas of land, so that he can dispose off the property.
Infact, the claimants 9 and 19 failed to make out any case to show that T.M.
Rangegowda L.A.C. No.45/2015 has any disposable/saleable right over the aforesaid property.
Under such circumstances, any agreement between T.M. Rangegowda and Vunduvalli Satyanarayana in respect of property of the claimants 1 to 8 cannot be accepted.
Therefore, this court is of the humble opinion that the claimants 9 and 19 have failed to prove the acquisition of property as claimed by them under the sale agreements dated 17.10.2006 and 13.12.2006.
